questions.text: In which year was the United Nations founded?
questions.explanation: The United Nations was founded in 1945 after the Second World War, replacing the League of Nations.

questions.text: Where is the headquarters of the United Nations located?
questions.explanation: The UN's main headquarters is located in New York City, United States.

questions.text: The UN Charter was signed at a conference held in which city in 1945?
questions.explanation: The UN Charter was signed on 26 June 1945 at the San Francisco Conference.

questions.text: How many permanent members does the UN Security Council have?
questions.explanation: The Security Council has five permanent members: the United States, United Kingdom, France, Russia and China.

questions.text: What is the total number of member states on the UN Security Council?
questions.explanation: The Security Council has 15 members in total: 5 permanent members and 10 non-permanent members elected for two-year terms.

questions.text: The International Court of Justice is seated in which city?
questions.explanation: The ICJ, the principal judicial organ of the UN, sits at the Peace Palace in The Hague.

questions.text: UNESCO, headquartered in Paris, primarily promotes international cooperation in which fields?
questions.explanation: UNESCO's mandate covers education, natural and social sciences, culture, and communication.

questions.text: In which year was UNESCO established?
questions.explanation: UNESCO's constitution was adopted in London in November 1945, the year of its founding.

questions.text: The World Health Organization is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: WHO, the UN's public health agency, is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.text: In which year was the World Health Organization established?
questions.explanation: WHO's constitution came into force on 7 April 1948, now observed annually as World Health Day.

questions.text: In which year was UNICEF established to assist children after the Second World War?
questions.explanation: The UN General Assembly created UNICEF in December 1946 to provide relief to children in war-affected countries.

questions.text: Where is UNICEF headquartered?
questions.explanation: UNICEF's headquarters is located in New York City.

questions.text: The UNHCR is the UN agency mandated to protect and assist which group of people?
questions.explanation: The Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees works to protect and assist refugees and displaced persons worldwide.

questions.text: In which year was the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees established?
questions.explanation: UNHCR was established by the UN General Assembly in December 1950.

questions.text: Which UN specialized agency, headquartered in Geneva, was founded in 1919 and is the oldest of its kind?
questions.explanation: The International Labour Organization was founded in 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles, making it the oldest specialized agency associated with the UN.

questions.text: The International Atomic Energy Agency, established in 1957, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The IAEA, the world's centre for nuclear cooperation, is headquartered in Vienna, Austria.

questions.text: The Food and Agriculture Organization is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The FAO, established in 1945 to lead efforts against hunger, is headquartered in Rome.

questions.text: Which international organization, founded in 1874 and headquartered in Bern, is considered the oldest international organization still in existence?
questions.explanation: The Universal Postal Union was established by the Treaty of Bern in 1874, predating the ILO and ITU as a formal permanent international body.

questions.text: How many official languages does the United Nations have?
questions.explanation: The UN has six official languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian and Spanish.

questions.text: In the UN General Assembly, how many votes does each member state hold?
questions.explanation: Under the principle of sovereign equality, every UN member state has exactly one vote in the General Assembly.

questions.text: In which year was the South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) established?
questions.explanation: SAARC was founded on 8 December 1985 in Dhaka.

questions.text: Where is the secretariat of SAARC located?
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat has been based in Kathmandu, Nepal, since 1987.

questions.text: How many member states does SAARC currently have?
questions.explanation: SAARC has eight member states after Afghanistan joined in 2007: Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, India, Maldives, Nepal, Pakistan and Sri Lanka.

questions.text: In which year was the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) established?
questions.explanation: The OIC was founded in 1969 following the Rabat Summit.

questions.text: Where is the headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation located?
questions.explanation: The OIC's headquarters is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, pending the liberation of Jerusalem.

questions.text: The Economic Cooperation Organization, headquartered in Tehran, was founded in 1985 by Iran, Pakistan and which other country?
questions.explanation: ECO was formed in 1985 by Iran, Pakistan and Turkey, building on the earlier Regional Cooperation for Development.

questions.text: In which year was the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) founded?
questions.explanation: ASEAN was founded in 1967 through the Bangkok Declaration, signed by Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand.

questions.text: The secretariat of ASEAN is located in which city?
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat is headquartered in Jakarta, Indonesia.

questions.text: In which year was the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) established?
questions.explanation: NATO was established in 1949 with the signing of the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington.

questions.text: Where is the headquarters of NATO located?
questions.explanation: NATO's headquarters has been located in Brussels, Belgium, since 1967.

questions.text: The main institutions of the European Union are headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: Brussels hosts the main EU institutions, including the European Commission and the Council of the EU.

questions.text: The African Union, headquartered in Addis Ababa, was established in 2002 as the successor to which organization?
questions.explanation: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity, which had been founded in 1963.

questions.text: The Commonwealth of Nations secretariat is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The Commonwealth Secretariat is based at Marlborough House in London.

questions.text: In which year was the League of Arab States founded?
questions.explanation: The Arab League was founded in Cairo in March 1945.

questions.text: The League of Arab States is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The Arab League's headquarters is located in Cairo, Egypt.

questions.text: In which year was the Gulf Cooperation Council established?
questions.explanation: The GCC was established in 1981 by Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, the UAE and Oman.

questions.text: The Shanghai Cooperation Organisation was established in which year?
questions.explanation: The SCO was founded in Shanghai in 2001 by China, Russia and four Central Asian states.

questions.text: The Organization of American States is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The OAS, founded in 1948, is headquartered in Washington D.C.

questions.text: In which year was the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) founded?
questions.explanation: OPEC was founded in Baghdad in September 1960.

questions.text: OPEC is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: OPEC's headquarters moved to Vienna, Austria, in 1965.

questions.text: The International Monetary Fund is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The IMF is headquartered in Washington D.C., alongside the World Bank.

questions.text: The IMF was established following which 1944 conference?
questions.explanation: The IMF and World Bank were both created at the 1944 Bretton Woods Conference in New Hampshire, USA.

questions.text: The World Bank is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The World Bank Group's headquarters is in Washington D.C.

questions.text: In which year was the World Bank established?
questions.explanation: The World Bank was established in 1944 at the Bretton Woods Conference, alongside the IMF.

questions.text: The World Trade Organization is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The WTO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.text: In which year did the World Trade Organization come into existence?
questions.explanation: The WTO was established on 1 January 1995, replacing the earlier GATT framework.

questions.text: The WTO succeeded which earlier trade agreement, signed in 1947?
options: General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade
questions.explanation: The General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT), signed in 1947, was the predecessor framework that the WTO replaced in 1995.

questions.text: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The Asian Development Bank is headquartered in Manila, Philippines.

questions.text: In which year was the Asian Development Bank established?
questions.explanation: The ADB was established in 1966 to promote economic development in Asia and the Pacific.

questions.text: The Bank for International Settlements, considered the world's oldest international financial institution, is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The BIS, founded in 1930, is headquartered in Basel, Switzerland.

questions.text: The Islamic Development Bank is headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The Islamic Development Bank is headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia.

questions.text: The Geneva Conventions primarily deal with which subject?
questions.explanation: The Geneva Conventions form the core of international humanitarian law, setting standards for the treatment of the wounded, prisoners and civilians in war.

questions.text: The four Geneva Conventions, forming the core of international humanitarian law, were adopted in which year?
questions.explanation: The four Geneva Conventions were adopted in 1949, updating earlier conventions dating back to 1864.

questions.text: The Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons (NPT) was opened for signature in which year?
questions.explanation: The NPT was opened for signature in 1968 and entered into force in 1970.

questions.text: The Non-Proliferation Treaty is primarily concerned with preventing the spread of which weapons?
questions.explanation: The NPT aims to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons and weapons technology.

questions.text: The Kyoto Protocol, adopted in 1997, primarily commits countries to reduce which type of emissions?
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol set binding targets for industrialized countries to reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

questions.text: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in which country?
questions.explanation: The Kyoto Protocol was adopted in Kyoto, Japan, in December 1997.

questions.text: The Paris Agreement, adopted in 2015, is an international treaty primarily addressing which issue?
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement is a legally binding international treaty on climate change mitigation and adaptation.

questions.text: The Paris Agreement was adopted at which UN climate conference?
questions.explanation: The Paris Agreement was adopted at COP21, held in Paris in December 2015.

questions.text: The Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, which codifies rules on diplomatic immunity, was adopted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations was adopted in 1961 and remains the basis of modern diplomatic law.

questions.text: The Peace of Westphalia, signed in 1648, is widely regarded as the origin of which modern concept?
questions.explanation: The Peace of Westphalia ended the Thirty Years' War and is credited with establishing the principle of state sovereignty that underpins the modern international system.

questions.text: The Treaty of Versailles, signed in 1919, formally ended which war?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Versailles formally ended the state of war between Germany and the Allied Powers after the First World War.

questions.text: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the UN General Assembly in which year?
questions.explanation: The UDHR was adopted by the UN General Assembly in Paris on 10 December 1948.

questions.text: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty was opened for signature in which year?
questions.explanation: The CTBT, which bans all nuclear explosions, was opened for signature in 1996.

questions.text: The Montreal Protocol, adopted in 1987, is an international treaty designed to protect which part of the environment?
questions.explanation: The Montreal Protocol phases out substances responsible for depleting the ozone layer.

questions.text: UNCLOS, adopted in 1982, is the principal international treaty governing which domain?
questions.explanation: The UN Convention on the Law of the Sea establishes the legal framework for maritime zones, navigation and resource rights.

questions.text: The Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, often called the 'treaty on treaties,' was adopted in which year?
questions.explanation: The Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties was adopted in 1969 and governs how treaties between states are made and interpreted.

questions.text: The Simla Agreement of 1972 was signed between Pakistan and which country?
questions.explanation: The Simla Agreement was signed between Pakistan and India in July 1972 following the 1971 war.

questions.text: The Tashkent Declaration of 1966 was signed by India and Pakistan following mediation by which country?
questions.explanation: The Tashkent Declaration was mediated by the Soviet Union after the 1965 India-Pakistan war.

questions.text: The Indus Waters Treaty of 1960 between India and Pakistan was brokered with the help of which institution?
questions.explanation: The World Bank facilitated negotiations and is a signatory guarantor of the Indus Waters Treaty.

questions.text: The Camp David Accords of 1978 led to a peace treaty between Egypt and which country?
questions.explanation: The Camp David Accords, brokered by US President Jimmy Carter, led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty.

questions.text: The 1988 Geneva Accords primarily addressed the withdrawal of Soviet troops from which country?
questions.explanation: The Geneva Accords, signed by Afghanistan, Pakistan, the US and the USSR, set the terms for Soviet troop withdrawal from Afghanistan.

questions.text: The Treaty of Lisbon, which reformed the institutional structure of the European Union, was signed in which year?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Lisbon was signed in 2007 and entered into force in 2009.

questions.text: The Maastricht Treaty, signed in 1992, formally established which organization?
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty created the European Union, replacing the earlier European Economic Community framework.

questions.text: The Schengen Agreement, signed in 1985, primarily allows for which of the following among participating European states?
options: Free movement without internal border checks
questions.explanation: The Schengen Agreement abolished internal border checks among signatory states, allowing free movement of people.

questions.text: The Chemical Weapons Convention is overseen by an organization headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, which implements the Chemical Weapons Convention, is headquartered in The Hague.

questions.text: The Biological Weapons Convention, the first multilateral treaty banning an entire category of weapons, opened for signature in which year?
questions.explanation: The Biological Weapons Convention opened for signature in 1972 and entered into force in 1975.

questions.text: The Rome Statute, adopted in 1998, established which international judicial body?
questions.explanation: The Rome Statute established the International Criminal Court, which began operating in 2002.

questions.text: The Kellogg-Briand Pact of 1928 committed signatory states to renounce which of the following?
options: War as an instrument of national policy
questions.explanation: The Kellogg-Briand Pact bound its signatories to renounce war as a means of resolving disputes.

questions.text: The Outer Space Treaty of 1967 establishes the basic legal framework governing which domain?
questions.explanation: The Outer Space Treaty of 1967 forms the basis of international space law, including the principle that space shall not be subject to national appropriation.
